notes: THE RECONCILIATION WINDOW, REBUILT. MATCH NOW SHOWS YOUR CHEQUES AND LODGEMENTS STRAIGHT AWAY. Opening MATCH on a statement line used to show an empty list unless you had first pressed PROPOSE MATCHES. Your cheques were in the register the whole time; the screen simply had not fetched them. They are now loaded with the statement lines, so Match always offers what is outstanding on that account. The list is ordered to be useful: anything for exactly the figure the bank printed comes first and is marked SAME AMOUNT, and the rest follow by date. An item you have just matched stops being offered immediately, so it cannot be picked twice. EVERY RECONCILING ITEM, NOT ONLY CHEQUES AND LODGEMENTS. A payment that leaves the bank without a cheque — a standing order, a direct debit, an ACH transfer, the paying leg of a bank transfer, a statutory remittance keyed as a journal — is a reconciling item, and the reconciliation lists it under LEFT THE BANK WITH NO CHEQUE. But Match only ever offered cheques and lodgements, so an amount sitting plainly on the statement AND in the ledger could not be matched to anything. The same was true of money that reached the bank with no lodgement. Match now offers all four. Matching one records the bank date against that ledger movement, which is exactly what the SHOWN button on the reconciliation does by hand, and unmatching takes the record away again. A bank date earlier than the day the ledger entered the movement is refused, with both dates named. WHEN MATCH HAS NOTHING TO OFFER, IT SAYS WHY. Match offers what is still outstanding, which is right: a cheque already presented cannot be presented again. But when the register had already cleared the item, the dialog simply came up empty, while the cheque sat in the register plainly bearing the same figure. On one real set of books, 31 of 37 open statement lines were in exactly that position, their cheques cleared in bulk at a month end before the statement was ever imported. Match now lists those under ALREADY CLEARED, SAME AMOUNT, naming the cheque or lodgement, the payee or payer, the amount, and the date it was settled. When there is genuinely nothing, the dialog says that too, and points at POST, which is what a charge the ledger has never seen actually needs. MATCH ANYWAY: CLEAR A CHEQUE ON THE DAY THE BANK SHOWS IT. Cheques are often cleared in bulk at a month end, before the statement arrives. The register then says 31 July while the bank says the 6th, and the cheque is no longer outstanding, so the statement line has nothing to match to. MATCH ANYWAY does both steps at once: it takes the clearance off, matches the line, and clears the item again on the bank date. The cheque or lodgement itself is untouched. Only the day it cleared changes, so it now leaves the reconciliation in the month the money actually moved. You are asked first, and the question names both dates: what the register says today, and what it will say afterwards. Only an ordinary clearance can be moved — a stale or cancelled cheque, or a lodgement closed on its own journal, is refused and sent to the register, where those consequences are visible. Everything runs through the register own paths, so every existing guard still applies. If anything stops the re-match part way, the original clearance goes back exactly as it was. A MONTH YOU HAVE SIGNED OFF IS NOW PROTECTED. A signed-off reconciliation is a filed record. Until now the register could still be changed underneath it, and the screen showed a drift warning only to whoever happened to reopen the month. Matching a statement line, unmatching it, Match anyway, posting a line as a charge or interest, reversing that posting, marking a ledger movement SHOWN, and booking an adjustment on the reconciliation are now all refused while the month stands signed off, and the refusal names the date: the reconciliation for 31 July is signed off, and a change dated 6 July would re-state it. Re-dating checks both months, the one the item clears in now and the one it would move to. The way back is unchanged and is your own: reopen that month on the Reconciliation screen and the change goes through. THE WINDOW LOOKS LIKE THE REST OF THE APP. The statement workbench came from the cash book apps and asked for styling this app had retired, so its table, its buttons and its dialogs were drawn with no styling at all. That is why the MATCH, POST and IGNORE keys looked wrong and the dialogs sat oddly on the page. It now uses the same table, buttons and panels as every other screen. While fixing it: the PRINT / PDF and EXPORT EXCEL buttons on the reconciliation, the general ledger and receipts were unstyled for the same reason, and are now correct. A statement line also says what it is, in words: MATCHED with the cheque number and payee, POSTED with the kind and the voucher code, SET ASIDE with your note, or OPEN with the proposal underneath. INSTALLING: no data changes. This installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first: Backup & Export, Back up now.
